title: Inherited regression intake and historical intent reconstruction
policy: No failure is dismissed as 'pre-existing'. Every failure is root-caused, classified, and assigned a resolution before any code changes.

cause_A.name: Installation outputs treated as installation prerequisites
cause_A.statement: Both bin/saathi-local `_check_env` and saathi/platform/private_alpha/prepare.py classify the repository-root build artifacts `.venv` and `saathi-os/node_modules` as REQUIRED prerequisites whose absence is a hard, unconditional FAIL. These are outputs of installation, not preconditions of it. On any checkout where installation has not yet been performed in place — a fresh clone, a git worktree, a clean-clone certification run, or a brand-new invited tester's machine — every downstream surface is blocked before it can execute.

evidence.method: Symlinked the primary worktree's .venv and saathi-os/node_modules into the M336-M343 worktree and re-ran the three suites.
evidence.after: 1 failed, 54 passed (only the release-gate failure, RC-B, remained)
evidence.conclusion: 7 of 8 inherited failures are fully explained by the absence of repository-root build artifacts; none of them is an implementation regression in platform, identity, mission, approval or observability logic.

cause_B.name: Release-gate secret scan cannot distinguish a bare PEM marker from real key material
cause_B.statement: saathi/ops/release_gate.py counts any `private_key_block` rule hit as a strong credential leak. The rule matches the PEM header alone (`-----BEGIN (RSA |EC |OPENSSH )?PRIVATE KEY-----`) with no requirement for a key body. Two security-control modules embed that header literal as intentional non-secret material — a rejection sample proving the payload sanitiser refuses private keys, and a detector pattern definition. The gate's only exclusion is a path prefix filter (`tests/`, `docs/`), which does not cover security-control source, so the gate returns EXIT_SECURITY (3).

evidence.hit_1: saathi/platform/tg/broker_readiness/security.py:100 — {"private_key": "-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----\nMIIE"} inside _secret_rejection_check() sample set
evidence.hit_2: saathi/platform/tg/integration_assurance/security.py:114 — re.compile(r"-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----\n[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{100,}") pattern definition
evidence.note: Neither hit contains base64 key body. Both are deliberately-planted markers belonging to the safety machinery itself.

failures.assertion: assert "BLOCKER" in r.stdout and "NOT ready" in r.stdout
failures.current_actual:
stdout is '  ! python venv missing at .venv ...
  ! frontend deps missing ...
environment not ready; see doctor
' (exit 1)
failures.expected: start reaches the readiness decision layer, reuses the healthy external backend PID 1782, reports a frontend BLOCKER naming the external PID, states no external process was killed, and exits non-zero
failures.first_known_failing_ancestor: 40617b5 — fix(platform): M57.1 launcher fail-closed readiness contract (2026-07-25 18:36 +0545). The SAATHI_LOCAL_ASSESS_* test seam was introduced 37 minutes after `_check_env` landed in 1919acf and was authored on a machine where .venv and saathi-os/node_modules already existed, so the preflight gate was never observed. The test has never passed on a checkout without build artifacts.
failures.related_milestone: M57 / M57.1 — localhost daily-use hardening and launcher fail-closed readiness contract
failures.historical_documentation: docs/platform/M57_PROCESS_MANAGEMENT.md:12 — 'Resolves the repo, verifies the Python venv + frontend deps, checks ports 8765 and 3000. If a healthy SaathiOS process already serves a port, it is reused and left as-is.'
failures.architecture_intent: The launcher verifies the Python venv and frontend deps because it may need to SPAWN `.venv/bin/python -m uvicorn` and `npm run dev`. When a role resolves to an already-healthy process (owned or external), the launcher spawns nothing and needs neither toolchain. The documented reuse path and the unconditional preflight contradict each other.
failures.test_or_implementation_stale: IMPLEMENTATION — the preflight is over-broad relative to documented intent; the test's assertions are correct and must be preserved verbatim
failures.safety_relevance: HIGH — this is the fail-closed contract that guarantees no external process is ever killed and that `start` never claims readiness it cannot prove. The current behaviour also emits a misleading blocker (reports a missing venv when the real blocker is an unhealthy frontend), degrading operator remediation.
failures.launch_relevance: HIGH — a private-alpha tester reusing an already-running SaathiOS instance is gated on developer build artifacts
failures.proposed_resolution: Make `_check_env` role-conditional: require the Python venv only when the launcher must spawn the backend (assessed state == free) and `saathi-os/node_modules` only when it must spawn the frontend. Preserve the hard fail-closed abort on the spawn paths. Do not modify the test.

failures.assertion: assert r.returncode == 0 and "SaathiOS localhost is ready" in r.stdout
failures.expected: both roles assessed external-healthy → start exits 0 and reports ready
failures.architecture_intent: Canonical final gate: report READY only if BOTH roles resolve healthy. Reuse of two healthy external processes is an explicitly supported, spawn-free path.
failures.safety_relevance: MEDIUM — the positive arm of the readiness contract; without it the negative arms cannot be proven exclusive
failures.launch_relevance: HIGH — this is the ordinary tester start path

failures.assertion: assert "UNRELATED PID 99999" in r.stdout and "refusing to kill" in r.stdout
failures.current_actual: returncode 1 for the wrong reason; the unrelated-occupant blocker is never printed
failures.expected: port 8765 held by an unrelated PID → explicit refusal to kill, fail-closed exit
failures.historical_documentation: docs/platform/M57_PROCESS_MANAGEMENT.md — 'If a port is held by an unrelated process, the launcher fails closed and never kills it.'
failures.architecture_intent: PID-safety is the launcher's strongest guarantee. The unrelated-occupant refusal must be reachable and must be the reported reason.
failures.safety_relevance: CRITICAL — masking the PID-safety refusal behind a generic environment error means the safety message operators depend on is never surfaced
failures.proposed_resolution: Same repair as index 1. The role-conditional preflight also guarantees the unrelated-occupant refusal is reported before any toolchain complaint, because a non-free port never reaches the spawn path.

failures.assertion: assert r1["ok"] is True (after prepare(install_deps=False) run twice)
failures.current_actual: ok=False; required checks python_venv='.venv missing' and frontend_deps='saathi-os/node_modules missing' both FAIL
failures.expected: prepare() is re-runnable, reports ok, creates required directories idempotently and never collects secrets
failures.first_known_failing_ancestor: 06e02b5 — feat(alpha): certify SaathiOS private-alpha release (M157–M165) (2026-07-29 12:55 +0545). prepare() shipped with python_venv and frontend_deps as required=True on the same commit as the test; the test has only ever passed on a checkout where installation had already been performed in place.
failures.architecture_intent: prepare() is the private-alpha INSTALLER preflight. It exists to tell an invited tester what to do next and to create required local directories safely, without collecting secrets. Reporting a missing venv is correct and must be preserved; treating that report as an unrecoverable required FAIL turns the installer into a surface that can never succeed on a machine that has not already been installed.
failures.test_or_implementation_stale: IMPLEMENTATION — the check reporting is correct, its aggregation into `ok` is not
failures.safety_relevance: MEDIUM — the assertions this test guards (no secrets collected, no paid providers, production_authorized=false, symlink rejection on required dirs) never execute past the ok assertion
failures.launch_relevance: CRITICAL — this is the first command an invited private-alpha tester runs
failures.proposed_resolution: Separate host prerequisites from installable build artifacts. `.venv` and `saathi-os/node_modules` become a distinct `installable` check class surfaced as a new deterministic field `install_complete`, still reported with full remediation text and still FAIL-status entries. `ok` continues to reflect every genuine host prerequisite (OS/arch, node, npm, disk, public-bind posture, config validity, database dir, symlink rejection, secret/provider/production posture). No check is deleted, no remediation is dropped, and no status is downgraded to PASS.

failures.assertion: assert r["ok"] is True for init_first_run(acknowledge_local_only=True, platform=platform, ...)
failures.expected: first-run onboarding completes idempotently, writes config, marks first_run_completed, never collects API credentials
related_source_files: saathi/platform/private_alpha/prepare.py line 346-348 (init_first_run early return on prepare failure)
failures.architecture_intent: init_first_run must refuse to proceed on a genuinely unsafe or unsupported host, and must require explicit local-only acknowledgement. It must not refuse merely because dependencies have not been installed yet.
failures.safety_relevance: MEDIUM — the local-only acknowledgement gate and 'no API credentials collected' posture are unreachable
failures.launch_relevance: CRITICAL — onboarding is step 2 of the private-alpha journey
failures.proposed_resolution: init_first_run continues to hard-refuse when host prerequisites fail. It additionally reports install completeness so an operator is told to install dependencies rather than being blocked with an opaque PREPARE_FAILED. The acknowledge_local_only refusal is unchanged.

failures.assertion: assert r["ok"] is True for apply_local_upgrade(fixture_dir=fix, work_db=db)
failures.expected: local fixture upgrade runs preflight → backup → config migration → smoke re-prepare → commit, with remote_fetch false throughout
failures.architecture_intent: The upgrade flow must never fetch remote releases and must be able to roll back. Its preflight guards disk headroom and host health.
failures.safety_relevance: HIGH — the backup-before-upgrade and rollback paths, and the remote_fetch=false assertion, are never exercised
failures.launch_relevance: HIGH — the rollback runbook depends on this flow
failures.proposed_resolution: upgrade_preflight and the post-migration smoke both consume the corrected prepare() contract. Disk-headroom gating and remote_fetch=false are unchanged.

failures.current_actual: fail_count == 1 — the single FAIL is check 'installation_prepare'
failures.expected: no FAIL checks; verdict PRIVATE_ALPHA_READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS with production_authorized and public_exposure_authorized both false
failures.architecture_intent: The M165 gate certifies private-alpha readiness across release integrity, lifecycle safety, public-listener scan, config posture, DR drill, support-bundle privacy, automation authority and incident playbooks. All other 20+ checks pass today.
failures.safety_relevance: HIGH — a permanently red gate cannot signal a real regression; the gate has been unable to reach a clean state since it shipped
failures.proposed_resolution: The installation_prepare check consumes the corrected prepare() contract, and install completeness is surfaced as its own explicit certification check so an incomplete installation is still visible in the report rather than silently dropped.

failures.expected: the safe gates (storage/config/db/backup/secret) pass; restore_verified true; secret_scan clean
failures.first_known_failing_ancestor: 79d3c29 — feat(tg): read-only broker readiness backend (M224–M231) and sandbox baseline (2026-07-30 07:29 +0545). Verified by `git log -S'BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY' -- saathi/`: 79d3c29 is the first commit introducing a PEM header literal into a tracked, non-test, non-doc file under saathi/. A second literal followed in 1e3f0a1 (M232–M239). The gate policy itself dates from bac5f9d (M13.5, 2026-07-11) and was correct until those modules landed.
failures.historical_documentation: In-source policy comment: 'counts strong-credential rules only; test fixtures + docs excluded'
failures.architecture_intent: The release gate must block a release when real credential material is committed. Its stated policy already acknowledges that intentional non-secret literals exist and must be excluded — it simply implements that exclusion as a coarse path-prefix filter that predates the existence of security-control modules carrying rejection samples.
failures.is_the_failure_correct: NO — the gate is firing on its own safety machinery. Neither hit is credential material: the rule matches a bare PEM header with no key body.
failures.documentation_conflict: None. No document claims the release gate is green; M328–M335 recorded it as an open inherited failure.
failures.generated_evidence_stale: NO — the scan is recomputed live from `git ls-files` on every run.
failures.obsolete_status_source: NO — the gate reads live repository state, not a cached status file.
failures.test_or_implementation_stale: IMPLEMENTATION — the detector's precision, not the test's expectation
failures.safety_relevance: CRITICAL — a permanently red security gate is indistinguishable from a real leak and trains operators to ignore it
failures.launch_relevance: CRITICAL — the release gate is the last automated barrier before a private-alpha release
failures.proposed_resolution: Raise the gate's precision instead of widening its exclusions. A `private_key_block` hit is counted as a strong credential only when actual key material follows the PEM header (base64 body of >= 100 characters, matching the standard already used by integration_assurance/security.py). A bare marker with no body is recorded as a non-material marker and reported in the gate output rather than silently dropped. Path-prefix exclusions are NOT widened, and no file is added to an allowlist. A focused regression test proves a real PEM key body still returns EXIT_SECURITY.

note_on_test_integrity: All eight failing assertions are correct expressions of the documented architectural intent. M337 resolves every failure in implementation only. No test file among the eight is edited, skipped, xfailed, deleted, or weakened; new focused regression tests are added alongside them.

documentation_drift_identified.issue: 'Resolves the repo, verifies the Python venv + frontend deps, checks ports' reads as an unconditional precondition and does not state that the reuse path spawns nothing and therefore needs neither toolchain.
documentation_drift_identified.action: Clarify in M337 to describe the role-conditional preflight precisely.
